confirmed_defect: Current1.1 applies P even valence to the symmetric-difference access path. That path is not an edge-subgraph of P; the stated cycle decomposition therefore does not follow.
repair: Replace1.1 only: decompose finite even-degree P into edge-disjoint simple graph cycles; use alpha*beta^{-1} only as a closed transverse test path with traversal multiplicity. Round each graph cycle near vertices in disks disjoint from the test path. Actual Jordan separation forces an even intersection count with every graph cycle. Edge-disjoint coverage then forces the total parity difference to vanish.
finite_details_checked: An unused-edge walk in a finite nonempty even-degree graph cannot end before a vertex repeats; the segment at the first repetition is a simple cycle. Removing it leaves every degree even, including loops, and deletes at least one edge.

Cycles may share vertices, but their open edges partition P; the test path avoids all vertices. Rounding cycles individually in vertex disks disjoint from the compact test-path image preserves all intersection counts.

The test path may self-intersect or retrace an arc. Jordan side changes count traversal events, so a complete closed traversal still has even count. No unjustified decomposition of the test path into graph cycles is used.

The endpoint inside a complementary region is immaterial because two such points can be joined inside that region without crossing P. Finite choices and finite generic perturbations add no choice axiom.
The vertex-free connected circle case is already one Jordan cycle; no positive-crossing assumption is inserted. Phase2.1 still gives adjacency and uniqueness up to swapping colors.
